correctness.rationale: The 20-vertex graph and face test are explicitly defined. Exhaustive and independent face constructors both give 63,143 faces. A deterministic 31,570-pair cover matching has exactly two critical cells in dimensions 0 and 6. Reversing exactly the matched Hasse arrows and topologically sorting all 63,142 nonempty faces and 410,500 incidences proves acyclicity. The discrete Morse theorem then gives a CW model with one 0-cell and one 6-cell, hence S^6 integrally; no homology-field assumption is used.

value.rationale: The dodecahedral graph is a canonical Platonic-solid cubic graph. The exact homotopy type at the first higher-independence parameter is not predictable from ordinary dodecahedral independence or matching homology. Its complex has 510 maximal faces in dimensions 7, 8, 9 and 11, yet is homotopy equivalent to a single 6-sphere. This is a natural complete finite classification that offers a nonpure high-dimensional benchmark rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
